newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady-off, feeders steady-up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady-off, feeders steady-up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle were called steady to up 0.150 cent per lb, livestock analysts said.

Reports that packers have pulled back on their bids for fed cattle after active buying from feedlots early in the week was expected to weigh on live cattle futures. Sources said there was very good movement for a holiday week but packers now appear to have adequate supplies to meet kills.
Boxed beef trade also slowed Tuesday afternoon which may weigh on sentiment, they said.

Feeder cattle futures were seen showing carryover strength following another gain in the latest CME feeder cattle index and expected further weakness in corn futures. Feeder supplies have been tight and declining feed costs have encouraged continued good interest for feeders, analysts said.
However, the market appears to be nearing a top especially with the nearby August approaching the 82.000-cent area. Corn futures may also be approaching a near-term bottom, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index climbed $0.27 to $80.57 per cwt, the highest level since April 19, 1994.
